course_name_original: Almacenamiento y Recuperación de Energía en Sistemas Eléctricos de Potencia y Vehículos Hibridos/Eléctricos (HEV/EV)
course_name_en: Energy Storage and Recovery in Electrical Power Systems and Hybrid/Electric Vehicles (HEV/EV)
prerequisites: Knowledge about digital control devices, such as DSC, DSPs, Microcontrollers
Basic software knowledge as Mathcad, Mathlab, Excel

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.

Writing, communicating and presenting scientific documents to specialists, within the scope of the contents of the Master Degree (electric power systems, hybrid and electrical vehicles and renewable energies)
Knowledge of the principal mathematic tools used in the analysis, modelling and simulation of power systems.
Use of computers and digital processors in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control and supervision of power systems.
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies and the constructive elements and materials of the Electrical Power Systems
Acquire the basic knowledge of power electronics to analyse and design electrical power systems
Understanding the fundamental characteristics, as well as advantages and drawbacks of electrical and hybrid traction systems compared to combustion engines
Ability to understand the necessity for systems and strategies of energy storage and recovery in electrical and hybrid vehicles (for the Scientific – Technological Research Strand only)
Technical-economical-environmental regulations and directives in different scopes (local, regional, national, European, etc.), which are applied to power systems
Understanding the needs of energy storage in electric / hybrid vehicles and power systems.
To analyze the different energy storage technologies in electric / hybrid vehicles and power systems.
To integrate energy sources in the power structure of the vehicle or power system.
To design the control system taking into account the characteristics of the power source.
To understand the rules governing the power system design.

syllabus_topics: Comparison between technologies (Pb-Acid, Ni-Cd, Ni-MH, Li-Ion)
Introduction to hydrogen production from renewable
Fuel cells: fuel cell vehicle topologies and system efficiencies
Energy management in EV and HEV
Specifications on EV, HEV, PHEV (plug-in hybrid electric vehicles) and PPHEV (plug-in, plug-out hybrid electric vehicles)
Use of energy storage technologies in electric traction drives
Design of the power stage (Switches selection, heat sink calculus, driver selection
Design of reactive elements: Input & output filter

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to at least 90% of the classes

assessment_rules: To evaluate the subject, it will be necessary to attend at least to 90% of the classes, which accounts for 5% of the final mark in every part. Several tasks will be proposed (30%-60%) and a simple group project (20%-60%). Optionally, an exam (up to 40%) can be proposed. To pass the subject, a minimum mark of 2.5 (over ten) is required in each part: Batteries, Hydrogen, Flywheels, Energy Management, and Resonant Inverter Design & Caps and Super Caps. The final mark will be calculated as (batteries + Flywheels + Hydrogen + Energy Managment + 2*Resonant inverter) / 6, provided that all individual marks are > 2.5.
